newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trelleborg may spin off Boliden - paper.
newsitem.headline: Trelleborg may spin off Boliden - paper.

text.p: Swedish miner Trelleborg is readying to list its mining and metals company, Boliden, on the Stockholm bourse, a Swedish financial newspaper said on Thursday.
Dagens Industri said preparations were already underway to list Boliden.
Rumours of a possible Boliden spin-off drove Trelleborg shares prices higher in the first few days of 1997, the paper said.
Trelleborg shares closed at 97 crowns on Wednesday, a rise of seven percent since the start of the year.

Boliden, a leading mining and metals company in Sweden, had sales worth 8.6 billion crowns in 1995 and accounted for nearly half of the Trelleborg group's total profit during the first nine months of last year.
Dagens Industri said the spin-off would be one way for Trelleborg managing director Kjell Nilsson to boost the value of the parent company.
Trelleborg reported a worse-than-expected profit for the first nine months of 1996.
The paper said Trelleborg declined to comment on the possibility of a Boliden sell-off.
